1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: In you come, sir, in you come,—you and your friends,

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Holmes fought three rounds with McMurdo at Alison's rooms.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: Don’t you remember the amateur who fought three rounds with you at Alison’s rooms on the night of your benefit four years back?

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: Thaddeus Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: Thaddeus Sholto was the last person who saw Bartholomew Sholto alive.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: I was the last person who saw him!

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.subject: treasure
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.statement: The treasure was stolen from Bartholomew Sholto.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-05-the-tragedy.quote: They have robbed him of the treasure!

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: One intruder's name is Jonathan Small.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: His name, I have every reason to believe, is Jonathan Small.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Jonathan Small's right leg is off.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: He is a poorly-educated man, small, active, with his right leg off, and wearing a wooden stump which is worn away upon the inner side.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.value: coarse, square-toed sole, with an iron band round the heel
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Jonathan Small's left boot has a coarse, square-toed sole with an iron band round the heel.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: His left boot has a coarse, square-toed sole, with an iron band round the heel.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: He is a middle-aged man, much sunburned, and has been a convict.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Number One entered via the trap-door to the roof.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: This, then, is the way by which Number One entered.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes discovers prints of a naked foot in the garret.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: The floor was covered thickly with the prints of a naked foot,—clear, well defined, perfectly formed, but scarce half the size of those of an ordinary man.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Number One
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Number One trod in the creosote.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: Number One has had the misfortune to tread in the creosote.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes found a thorn driven into the dead man's scalp.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: As you saw, I discovered a thorn which had been driven or shot with no great force into the scalp.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Thaddeus Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: The dead man died from a powerful vegetable alkaloid poison.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: Death from some powerful vegetable alkaloid,

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Athelney Jones
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Athelney Jones arrests Thaddeus Sholto for being concerned in the death of his brother.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: I arrest you in the Queen’s name as being concerned in the death of your brother.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Miss Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Miss Morstan lives with Mrs. Cecil Forrester in Lower Camberwell.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: She lives with Mrs. Cecil Forrester, in Lower Camberwell: so it is not very far.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Watson is sent to fetch Toby the dog from Sherman.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: You will bring Toby back in the cab with you.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Toby
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: I know a dog that would follow that scent to the world’s end.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: jewels
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: The missing jewels are worth half a million.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: Jewels worth half a million missing.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.statement: Holmes opens the trap-door leading out onto the roof.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-06-sherlock-ho.quote: This is a trap-door which leads out on to the roof.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Watson escorted Miss Morstan back to her home in a cab.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: The police had brought a cab with them, and in this I escorted Miss Morstan back to her home.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Miss Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Miss Morstan burst into a passion of weeping in the cab.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: In the cab, however, she first turned faint, and then burst into a passion of weeping,—so sorely had she been tried by the adventures of the night.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Mrs. Forrester
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Mrs. Forrester opened the door herself to Miss Morstan and Watson.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: She opened the door herself, a middle-aged, graceful woman, and it gave me joy to see how tenderly her arm stole round the other’s waist and how motherly was the voice in which she greeted her.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Miss Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Mrs. Forrester is an honoured friend to Miss Morstan, not a paid dependant.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: She was clearly no mere paid dependant, but an honoured friend.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Watson returned to Pondicherry Lodge with Toby.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: It had just struck three on the Palace clock when I found myself back once more at Pondicherry Lodge.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: McMurdo
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: McMurdo was arrested as an accessory and marched to the station with Mr. Sholto.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: The ex-prize-fighter McMurdo had, I found, been arrested as an accessory, and both he and Mr. Sholto had been marched off to the station.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes was standing on the door-step at Pondicherry Lodge smoking his pipe.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Holmes was standing on the door-step, with his hands in his pockets, smoking his pipe.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes found a small pocket or pouch woven of coloured grasses with tawdry beads.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: The object which he held up to me was a small pocket or pouch woven out of coloured grasses and with a few tawdry beads strung round it.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Holmes climbed down onto the water-barrel and then to the earth.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Then with a light spring he came on to the barrel, and from there to the earth.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Toby
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Toby raced through the timber-yard and sprang upon a large barrel on a hand-trolley.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: On the dog raced through sawdust and shavings, down an alley, round a passage, between two wood-piles, and finally, with a triumphant yelp, sprang upon a large barrel which still stood upon the hand-trolley on which it had been brought.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Jonathan Small is the wooden-legged man.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: Therefore we may say with confidence that the wooden-legged man is identical with Jonathan Small.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.statement: Jonathan Small drew a map of the buried treasure for the two officers.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-07-the-episode.quote: A map is drawn for them by an Englishman named Jonathan Small.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Aurora
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: The steam launch Aurora is owned by Mordecai Smith.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: I want to find the whereabouts of a steam launch called the _Aurora_, owner Mordecai Smith, black with two red streaks, funnel black with a white band.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Aurora
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: The Aurora's hull is black with two red streaks.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: She’s been fresh painted, black with two red streaks.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Aurora
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: The Aurora's funnel is black with a white band.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Mordecai Smith
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Mordecai Smith has been away since yesterday morning.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: He’s been away since yesterday mornin’, sir, and, truth to tell, I am beginnin’ to feel frightened about him.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Mordecai Smith
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Mordecai Smith left in the steam launch Aurora.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: it is in the steam launch that he has gone.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: wooden-legged man
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: The wooden-legged man roused Mordecai Smith up in the night.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: It was him that roused him up yesternight, and, what’s more, my man knew he was comin’, for he had steam up in the launch.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Toby
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Toby tracked the scent to the edge of the wharf at the water.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: Toby led us to the very edge of this, and there stood whining, looking out on the dark current beyond.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes sent a wire to his lieutenant Wiggins.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: That wire was to my dirty little lieutenant, Wiggins, and I expect that he and his gang will be with us before we have finished our breakfast.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Wiggins
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: In future they can report to you, Wiggins, and you to me.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes instructs the boys to watch Mordecai Smith's landing-stage for the Aurora's return.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: I want one boy to be at Mordecai Smith’s landing-stage opposite Millbank to say if the boat comes back.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes paid each of the Baker Street irregulars a shilling in advance.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: He handed them a shilling each, and away they buzzed down the stairs, and I saw them a moment later streaming down the street.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Bartholomew Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: Mr. Bartholomew Sholto, of Pondicherry Lodge, Upper Norwood, was found dead in his room under circumstances which point to foul play.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Thaddeus Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: the brother, Thaddeus Sholto, has already been arrested, together with the housekeeper, Mrs. Bernstone, an Indian butler named Lal Rao, and a porter, or gatekeeper, named McMurdo.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Jonathan Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Jonathan Small came from the Andamans.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: we had already determined that Small had come from the Andamans

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Jim
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Jim is Mrs. Smith's eldest child.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: My old man woke up Jim,—that’s my eldest,—and away they went, without so much as a word to me.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Watson is at Baker Street for bath and breakfast.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: A bath at Baker Street and a complete change freshened me up wonderfully.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.statement: Holmes plays his violin to put Watson to sleep.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-08-the-baker-s.quote: he began to play some low, dreamy, melodious air

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Wiggins
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Wiggins reported that no trace of the launch could be found.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: He says that no trace can be found of the launch.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes said he must remain on guard to wait for a message.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: but I must remain on guard.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Watson went to Camberwell to call upon Mrs. Cecil Forrester.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: Then I shall run over to Camberwell and call upon Mrs. Cecil Forrester.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Watson left Toby with a half-sovereign at the old naturalist's in Pinchin Lane.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: I took our mongrel accordingly, and left him, together with a half-sovereign, at the old naturalist’s in Pinchin Lane.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Watson told the ladies of Mr. Sholto's death but said nothing of the exact manner and method of it.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: although I spoke of Mr. Sholto’s death, I said nothing of the exact manner and method of it.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes left to go down the river.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: I am off down the river, Watson,

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Watson remained as Holmes's representative to open all notes and telegrams.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: I want you to open all notes and telegrams, and to act on your own judgment if any news should come.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Mordecai Smith
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Mordecai Smith and his son Jim left Smith's Wharf at about three o'clock last Tuesday morning in the steam launch Aurora.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: Mordecai Smith, boatman, and his son, Jim, left Smith’s Wharf at or about three o’clock last Tuesday morning in the steam launch _Aurora_,

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes placed the lost advertisement about Mordecai Smith and the Aurora.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Thaddeus Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Thaddeus Sholto and Mrs. Bernstone were both released yesterday evening.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: He and the housekeeper, Mrs. Bernstone, were both released yesterday evening.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Jones
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Jones asked Holmes for assistance because his case had come to nothing.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: I should be very glad of a little assistance.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes worked all day disguised as an aged seaman.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: I have been working in that get-up all day,

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Holmes requested a fast police-boat to be at the Westminster Stairs at seven o'clock.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: I shall want a fast police-boat—a steam launch—to be at the Westminster Stairs at seven o’clock.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.statement: Half of the treasure rightfully belongs to Mary.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-09-a-break-in-.quote: to the young lady to whom half of it rightfully belongs.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes filled up three glasses with port.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: Holmes glanced at his watch, and filled up three glasses with port.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes ordered a cab for half-past six.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: I ordered it for half-past six.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes ordered the green lamp marking the police-boat to be taken off.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes ordered the launch to stop opposite Jacobson's Yard.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: Tell them to stop opposite Jacobson’s Yard.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: A wooden-legged man handed the Aurora over to Jacobson's Yard two days ago.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: I learned that the _Aurora_ had been handed over to them two days ago by a wooden-legged man, with some trivial directions as to her rudder.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Mordecai Smith
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Mordecai Smith demanded the Aurora for eight o'clock that night.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: I want her to-night at eight o’clock,

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes stationed his boy as a sentry over the launch.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: I stationed him as a sentry over the launch.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Jones
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Jones yelled to the Aurora to stop.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: Jones yelled to them to stop.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Islander
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: The Islander plucked out a short round piece of wood and clapped it to his lips.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: Even as we looked he plucked out from under his covering a short, round piece of wood, like a school-ruler, and clapped it to his lips.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes fired his pistol at the Islander.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Watson fired his pistol at the Islander.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Islander
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: The Islander fell sideways into the stream.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: He whirled round, threw up his arms, and with a kind of choking cough fell sideways into the stream.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Small ran the launch up upon the mud-bank and his stump sank into the soil.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: The fugitive sprang out, but his stump instantly sank its whole length into the sodden soil.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Holmes
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Holmes's party hauled Small out of the mud and dragged him over their side.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: When we brought our launch alongside he was so firmly anchored that it was only by throwing the end of a rope over his shoulders that we were able to haul him out, and to drag him, like some evil fish, over our side.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: iron chest
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: The solid iron chest on the Aurora's deck had contained the Sholtos' treasure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: This, there could be no question, was the same that had contained the ill-omened treasure of the Sholtos.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Small's right leg is a wooden stump from the thigh downwards.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: I could see that from the thigh downwards there was but a wooden stump upon the right side.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Mordecai Smith
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: Mordecai Smith is the father of the boy with him on the Aurora.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: The two Smiths, father and son, sat sullenly in their launch, but came aboard meekly enough when commanded.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.subject: Islander
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.statement: The Islander is dead in the Thames.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-10-the-end-of-.quote: Somewhere in the dark ooze at the bottom of the Thames lie the bones of that strange visitor to our shores.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Small is about fifty years old.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: His age may have been fifty or thereabouts, for his black, curly hair was thickly shot with grey.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Tonga
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Tonga shot Sholto with one of his darts.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: It was that little hell-hound Tonga who shot one of his cursed darts into him.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Small struck Tonga with the slack end of the rope.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: I welted the little devil with the slack end of the rope for it, but it was done, and I could not undo it again.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Sholto usually went down to his supper at the time Small entered.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: I knew the habits of the house pretty well, and it was the time when Mr. Sholto usually went down to his supper.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Small climbed through the window and saw Sholto grinning with his head on his shoulder.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: I never got such a turn in my life as when I saw him grinning at me with his head on his shoulder as I climbed through the window.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Small is under the charge of Athelney Jones of Scotland Yard.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: You are under the charge of Mr. Athelney Jones, of Scotland Yard.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Vauxhall
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: The drive from Vauxhall to Mrs. Cecil Forrester's takes a quarter of an hour.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: A quarter of an hour’s drive brought us to Mrs. Cecil Forrester’s.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Esmeralda
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: The Esmeralda at Gravesend is outward bound for the Brazils.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: We told him nothing, but we paid him well, and he was to get something handsome if we reached our vessel, the _Esmeralda_, at Gravesend, outward bound for the Brazils.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Small threw the treasure-box key into the Thames.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: “Small threw it into the Thames,” I answered.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Mary
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.statement: Mary owns half of the Agra treasure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: Half of it is yours and half is Thaddeus Sholto’s.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.subject: Watson
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-11-the-great-a.quote: Because I love you, Mary, as truly as ever a man loved a woman.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small was born near Pershore.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I am a Worcestershire man myself,—born near Pershore.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.value: right leg just above the knee
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small's wound is his right leg just above the knee.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: A crocodile took me, just as I was half-way across, and nipped off my right leg as clean as a surgeon could have done it, just above the knee.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small served in the 3rd Buffs.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I got into a mess over a girl, and could only get out of it again by taking the Queen’s shilling and joining the 3rd Buffs, which was just starting for India.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small's employer was Abel White.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: A man named Abel White, who had come out there as an indigo-planter, wanted an overseer to look after his coolies and keep them up to their work.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: John Holder
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: John Holder is a company sergeant.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: my company sergeant, John Holder, was in the water at the same time, and he was one of the finest swimmers in the service.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Tonga
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Tonga is an Andaman Islander.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: One day when Dr. Somerton was down with a fever a little Andaman Islander was picked up by a convict-gang in the woods.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Morstan
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Morstan and Sholto are bosom friends.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: They were bosom friends, those two, and never far apart.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small tripped Achmet with his firelock as Achmet ran past.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I cast my firelock between his legs as he raced past, and he rolled twice over like a shot rabbit.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Dost Akbar
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Dost Akbar stabbed Achmet twice in the side.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: Ere he could stagger to his feet the Sikh was upon him, and buried his knife twice in his side.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small hid the treasure in a hollow under bricks in the Agra fort wall.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: We carried the box, therefore, into the same hall where we had buried the body, and there, under certain bricks in the best-preserved wall, we made a hollow and put our treasure.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small drew charts of the treasure hiding place signed with the sign of four.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I sat up all night with paper and ink, and by the morning I had the two charts all ready, signed with the sign of four,—that is, of Abdullah, Akbar, Mahomet, and myself.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Sholto
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Sholto stole all the treasure.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: The scoundrel had stolen it all, without carrying out one of the conditions on which we had sold him the secret.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small killed the convict-guard by striking him with his wooden leg.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: He put his carbine to his shoulder, but I struck him full, and knocked the whole front of his skull in.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small escaped from the Andamans by boat with Tonga.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I made for the boat, and in an hour we were well out at sea.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small pinned the sign of the four on Sholto's bosom.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: so I scrawled down the sign of the four of us, as it had been on the chart, and I pinned it on his bosom.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Tonga
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Tonga killed Bartholomew Sholto.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: Tonga thought he had done something very clever in killing him, for when I came up by the rope I found him strutting about as proud as a peacock.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small took the treasure-box down from Pondicherry Lodge and left the sign of the four on the table.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I took the treasure-box and let it down, and then slid down myself, having first left the sign of the four upon the table, to show that the jewels had come back at last to those who had most right to them.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small scattered the loot to hide it when the launch caught them.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: When I saw that your launch must catch us, I put the loot away in a safe place.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Small
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: Small engaged Smith to escape in his launch.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: I engaged with old Smith, and was to give him a big sum if he got us safe to our ship.

1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.subject: Agra treasure
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.statement: The Agra treasure contained one hundred and forty-three diamonds of the first water.
1890-the-sign-of-the-four-12-the-strange.quote: There were one hundred and forty-three diamonds of the first water, including one which has been called, I believe, ‘the Great Mogul’ and is said to be the second largest stone in existence.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene Adler
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Born in New Jersey in the year 1858.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene Adler
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene Adler was born in New Jersey.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Born in New Jersey in the year 1858.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene Adler
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.value: Prima donna Imperial Opera of Warsaw
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene Adler was Prima donna of the Imperial Opera of Warsaw.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Prima donna Imperial Opera of Warsaw—yes!

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: King of Bohemia
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: The King of Bohemia's full name is Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Your Majesty had not spoken before I was aware that I was addressing Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein, Grand Duke of Cassel-Felstein, and hereditary King of Bohemia.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene Adler
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.value: Briony Lodge, Serpentine Avenue, St. John’s Wood
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene Adler lives at Briony Lodge, Serpentine Avenue, St. John’s Wood.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: Is Briony Lodge, Serpentine Avenue, St. John’s Wood.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene Adler
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene Adler's spouse is Godfrey Norton.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: I was half-dragged up to the altar, and before I knew where I was I found myself mumbling responses which were whispered in my ear, and vouching for things of which I knew nothing, and generally assisting in the secure tying up of Irene Adler, spinster, to Godfrey Norton, bachelor.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Holmes
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Holmes witnesses the marriage of Irene Adler to Godfrey Norton.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: It seems that there had been some informality about their license, that the clergyman absolutely refused to marry them without a witness of some sort, and that my lucky appearance saved the bridegroom from having to sally out into the streets in search of a best man.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Watson
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Watson throws his smoke-rocket into the room at Holmes's signal.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: At the same instant I saw him raise his hand and at the signal I tossed my rocket into the room with a cry of “Fire!”

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: woman
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: When a woman thinks her house is on fire, her instinct is at once to rush to the thing she values most.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: When a woman thinks that her house is on fire, her instinct is at once to rush to the thing which she values most.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene Adler
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene Adler reveals the photograph hidden in a recess behind a sliding panel just above the right bell-pull.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: The photograph is in a recess behind a sliding panel just above the right bell-pull.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene Adler
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene Adler leaves England with her husband by the 5:15 train from Charing Cross for the Continent.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: She left this morning with her husband by the 5:15 train from Charing Cross for the Continent.

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: King of Bohemia
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: The King of Bohemia pays Holmes three hundred pounds in gold and seven hundred in notes.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: There are three hundred pounds in gold and seven hundred in notes,

1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.subject: Irene Adler
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.statement: Irene Adler keeps the photograph only to safeguard herself and preserve a weapon against future steps by the King.
1891-a-scandal-in-bohemia.md.quote: I keep it only to safeguard myself, and to preserve a weapon which will always secure me from any steps which he might take in the future.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: my grandfather had two sons—my uncle Elias and my father Joseph.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Joseph
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Joseph is the father of John Openshaw.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: I leave my estate, with all its advantages and all its disadvantages, to my brother, your father,

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Elias was a planter in Florida.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: became a planter in Florida, where he was reported to have done very well.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: During all the years that he lived at Horsham, I doubt if ever he set foot in the town.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: John Openshaw
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: I have lived happily at Horsham,

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Elias receives five dried orange pips in a letter.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: Opening it hurriedly, out there jumped five little dried orange pips, which pattered down upon his plate.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Joseph
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Joseph receives five dried orange pips in an envelope.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: There he was, sitting with a newly opened envelope in one hand and five dried orange pips in the outstretched palm of the other one.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: John Openshaw
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: John Openshaw receives five dried orange pips in an envelope.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: turning to the table he shook out upon it five little dried orange pips.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Elias burns his papers in his room.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: in the grate there was a mass of black, fluffy ashes, as of burned paper,

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Elias
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Elias is dead, found in a pool at the foot of the garden.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: We found him, when we went to search for him, face downward in a little green-scummed pool, which lay at the foot of the garden.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Joseph
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Joseph is dead after falling over a chalk-pit.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: My father had fallen over one of the deep chalk-pits which abound in the neighbourhood,

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: John Openshaw
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: John Openshaw is dead and his body was recovered from the water.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: It proved to be that of a young gentleman whose name, as it appears from an envelope which was found in his pocket, was John Openshaw, and whose residence is near Horsham.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Ku Klux Klan
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: The Ku Klux Klan's outrages are usually preceded by a warning such as orange pips.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: Its outrages were usually preceded by a warning sent to the marked man in some fantastic but generally recognised shape—a sprig of oak-leaves in some parts, melon seeds or orange pips in others.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: James Calhoun
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: James Calhoun is captain of the Lone Star.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: Captain James Calhoun, Barque _Lone Star_, Savannah, Georgia.

1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.subject: Holmes
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.statement: Holmes sends five orange pips to James Calhoun.
1891-the-five-orange-pips.md.quote: Of these he took five and thrust them into an envelope.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Elias Whitney
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Elias Whitney is the brother of Isa Whitney.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: brother of the late Elias Whitney, D.D., Principal of the Theological College of St. George’s

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Isa Whitney
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Isa Whitney is addicted to opium.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Isa Whitney
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Isa Whitney is the husband of Kate Whitney.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: It was not the first time that she had spoken to us of her husband’s trouble

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Isa Whitney
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Isa Whitney is at the Bar of Gold in Upper Swandam Lane.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: at the Bar of Gold, in Upper Swandam Lane.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Watson
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Watson is Isa Whitney's medical adviser.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: I was Isa Whitney’s medical adviser, and as such I had influence over him.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Watson
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Watson sends Isa Whitney home in a cab.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: In a few minutes I had written my note, paid Whitney’s bill, led him out to the cab, and seen him driven through the darkness.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Holmes
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Holmes is disguised as an old man in the opium den.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: and there, sitting by the fire and grinning at my surprise, was none other than Sherlock Holmes.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville St. Clair is thirty-seven years of age.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Mr. St. Clair is now thirty-seven years of age, is a man of temperate habits, a good husband, a very affectionate father, and a man who is popular with all who know him.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Mrs St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Mrs St. Clair sees her husband beckoning from a second-floor window.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: and was struck cold to see her husband looking down at her and, as it seemed to her, beckoning to her from a second-floor window.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Lascar
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: The Lascar pushes Mrs St. Clair out into the street.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: who thrust her back and, aided by a Dane, who acts as assistant there, pushed her out into the street.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: All of Neville St. Clair's clothes except his coat were found in the front room.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Thrust away behind a curtain in the front room were all the clothes of Mr. Neville St. Clair, with the exception of his coat.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: coat
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville St. Clair's coat pockets were stuffed with 421 pennies and 270 half-pennies.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: Every pocket stuffed with pennies and half-pennies—421 pennies and 270 half-pennies.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Hugh Boone
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Hugh Boone is a professional beggar.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: He is a professional beggar, though in order to avoid the police regulations he pretends to a small trade in wax vestas.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Hugh Boone
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Hugh Boone is Neville St. Clair in disguise.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: to Mr. Neville St. Clair, of Lee, in the county of Kent.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville St. Clair throws his weighted coat out of the window into the Thames.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: I hurled it out of the window, and it disappeared into the Thames.

1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.subject: Neville St. Clair
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.statement: Neville St. Clair writes a letter telling his wife not to be frightened.
1891-the-man-with-the-twisted-lip.md.quote: ‘Dearest do not be frightened. All will come well. There is a huge error which it may take some little time to rectify. Wait in patience.—NEVILLE.’

1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.subject: St Simon
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.value: Lord Robert Walsingham de Vere St. Simon
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.statement: St Simon's full name is Lord Robert Walsingham de Vere St. Simon.
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.quote: ‘Lord Robert Walsingham de Vere St. Simon, second son of the Duke of Balmoral.'

1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.subject: Aloysius
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.statement: Aloysius is the father of Hatty.
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.quote: Miss Hatty Doran, the only daughter of Aloysius Doran.

1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.subject: Frank
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.quote: that was my true wedding after all those years of waiting.

1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.subject: St Simon
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.statement: St Simon marries Hatty in a ceremony at St George's, Hanover Square.
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.quote: The ceremony, which was performed at St. George’s, Hanover Square, was a very quiet one, no one being present save the father of the bride, Mr. Aloysius Doran, the Duchess of Balmoral, Lord Backwater, Lord Eustace and Lady Clara St. Simon (the younger brother and sister of the bridegroom), and Lady Alicia Whittington.

1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.subject: Hatty
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.statement: Hatty drops her bouquet as she goes towards the vestry.
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.quote: She dropped her bouquet as we went towards the vestry.

1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.subject: Frank
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.statement: Frank writes Hatty a note in the church pew.
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.quote: Then I saw him scribble on a piece of paper, and I knew that he was writing me a note.

1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.subject: Hatty
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.statement: Hatty leaves the breakfast-room after sitting down for ten minutes.
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.quote: Then, after we had sat down for ten minutes or so, she rose hurriedly, muttered some words of apology, and left the room.

1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.subject: Hatty
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.statement: Hatty follows Frank into Hyde Park.
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.quote: He beckoned to me and then began walking into the Park.

1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.subject: Hatty
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.statement: Hatty goes to lodgings in Gordon Square with Frank.
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.quote: away we drove to some lodgings he had taken in Gordon Square, and that was my true wedding after all those years of waiting.

1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.subject: Flora
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.statement: Flora was formerly a danseuse at the Allegro.
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.quote: It appears that she was formerly a _danseuse_ at the Allegro, and that she has known the bridegroom for some years.

1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.subject: Flora
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.statement: Flora is arrested in connection with Hatty's disappearance.
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.quote: That Miss Flora Millar, the lady who had caused the disturbance, has actually been arrested.

1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.subject: Frank
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.statement: Frank had been a prisoner among the Apaches and escaped.
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.quote: Frank had been a prisoner among the Apaches, had escaped, came on to ’Frisco, found that I had given him up for dead and had gone to England, followed me there, and had come upon me at last on the very morning of my second wedding.

1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.subject: St Simon
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.statement: St Simon owns no property save the small estate of Birchmoor.
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.quote: as Lord St. Simon has no property of his own save the small estate of Birchmoor, it is obvious that the Californian heiress is not the only gainer by an alliance which will enable her to make the easy and common transition from a Republican lady to a British peeress.

1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.subject: Holmes
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.statement: Holmes invites the Moultons to meet St Simon at his rooms.
1892-the-adventure-of-the-noble-bachelor.quote: I invited them to meet him here, and, as you see, I made him keep the appointment.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Mycroft
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: “Because my brother Mycroft possesses it in a larger degree than I do.”

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Mycroft
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Mycroft is seven years senior to Sherlock.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Mycroft
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.value: audits the books in some of the government departments
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Mycroft audits the books in some of the government departments.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: He has an extraordinary faculty for figures, and audits the books in some of the government departments.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Mycroft
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: Mycroft lodges in Pall Mall, and he walks round the corner into Whitehall every morning and back every evening.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Diogenes Club
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Save in the Stranger's Room, no talking is allowed in the Diogenes Club.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: Save in the Stranger’s Room, no talking is, under any circumstances, allowed, and three offences, if brought to the notice of the committee, render the talker liable to expulsion.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Melas
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Melas is the chief Greek interpreter in London.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: For many years I have been the chief Greek interpreter in London, and my name is very well known in the hotels.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Latimer
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Latimer takes Melas in a cab with windows covered with paper to prevent him seeing where they drive.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: I found to my astonishment that they were covered with paper so as to prevent my seeing through them.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Latimer
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Latimer threatens Melas with serious consequences if he raises an alarm or acts against his interests.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: I must warn you, however, Mr. Melas, that if at any time to-night you attempt to raise an alarm or do anything which is against my interests, you will find it a very serious thing.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Kratides
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Kratides refuses to sign the papers unless he sees Sophy married in his presence by a Greek priest he knows.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: ‘Only if I see her married in my presence by a Greek priest whom I know.’

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Sophy
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Sophy recognizes Paul as her brother when she enters the room.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: ‘Harold,’ said she, speaking English with a broken accent.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Kemp
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: He imprudently puts himself into the power of the young man and his older associate.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Latimer
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Latimer and Kemp kept Kratides a prisoner and tried by cruelty and starvation to make him sign away his and his sister's property.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: These two, finding that through his ignorance of the language he was helpless in their hands, had kept him a prisoner, and had endeavoured by cruelty and starvation to make him sign away his own and his sister’s property.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Sophy
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Sophy is living at The Myrtles, Beckenham.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: She is living at present at The Myrtles, Beckenham.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Sherlock
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Sherlock and the others drag Melas out of the charcoal-filled room and revive him.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: With a rush we got to the poisoned men and dragged them out into the well-lit hall.

1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.subject: Kratides
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.statement: Kratides is dead when found at The Myrtles.
1893-the-greek-interpreter.md.quote: He had ceased to moan as we laid him down, and a glance showed me that for him at least our aid had come too late.
